label: fiction
title: The Seventh Page
setting: In a fictional state during an invented armed conflict, a defence-language specialist is accused of knowingly adding a protected negotiating limit to an otherwise authorised exchange with a hostile foreign authority.
charge: treason by assisting a hostile foreign power
elements: An armed conflict existed between the fictional state and a hostile foreign power.
The accused intentionally provided material assistance to that hostile power.
The accused knew the assistance would prejudice the fictional state’s security or defence.
hook: The judge enters as negotiations continue beyond the courthouse. Seven pages lie under glass. Six were cleared. The seventh exposed a protected limit. Sela Orr, a defence-language specialist charged with treason, accepts she edited it and sent the package. She denies knowing it travelled. The question is not what happened, but what she knew.

accused.human: Sela Orr, 51, is a defence-language specialist who maintains internal working drafts and has openly argued for more transparent peace negotiations.
accused.if_guilty: If convicted, sentencing would be decided separately by the judge. The jury's task is limited to deciding whether the prosecution proved the charge.

prosecution.speaker: pc
prosecution.text: You will hear that Sela Orr corrected a confidential negotiating limit, then confirmed a package bound for a hostile authority eleven minutes later. That authority used the limit at the next talks. The six approved briefs were lawful, and the system had a fault. The prosecution's case is that those facts do not explain this sequence: her timing, destination warning, and the advantage that followed.

defence.speaker: dc
defence.text: The six briefs were supposed to go: they were an authorised part of peace talks. Page seven was not. You will see a signed release sheet and confirmation screen listing six files. You will hear that the system could silently inherit a seventh, and that earlier support tickets recorded the fault. Sela's job required the corrections. A disastrous mistake is not treason; the question is what she knew.

prosecution.speaker: pc
prosecution.text: Put the sequence together. Sela knew whose account it was, corrected the one page that later gave the hostile negotiators an advantage, and clicked send eleven minutes later. Neri's work request explains the edit, but not necessarily Sela's next act. The fault shows how a file can travel, but it does not compel you to accept that this experienced specialist missed the link. The prosecution says intention and knowledge are proved.

defence.speaker: dc
defence.text: The harm is real, but hindsight isn't proof of treason. Neri asked Sela to correct the internal master; Halen built and approved the six-file package. The authenticated release sheet and confirmation screen listed those six lawful briefs, while a known fault silently carried page seven. Knowledge of the recipient proves only where Sela knew the authorised package was going. No record shows she saw the hidden attachment. That missing link is reasonable doubt.

epilogue: The language office disabled inherited attachments and required two people to compare every release sheet with the files actually sent. Negotiators later published a redacted review of the four-day delay without naming individual staff. Sela returned home to wait for the court process to end. Her colleagues kept the internal debate about secrecy separate from the technical failure. The armed conflict and the negotiations continued beyond this courtroom.

turns.speaker: w1

beats.speaker: w2

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Why were any briefs going to a hostile authority?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: We had an authorised channel for ceasefire wording. The six briefs contained language both teams were meant to see.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: What happened at the next negotiation?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: I heard their delegate quote our exact private ceiling and refuse further movement. We lost four days from an already narrow security-planning window.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Had that ceiling been cleared for release?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: No. It was protected.

beats.text: Why were any briefs going to a hostile authority? We had an authorised channel for ceasefire wording. The six briefs contained language both teams were meant to see. What happened at the next negotiation? I heard their delegate quote our exact private ceiling and refuse further movement. We lost four days from an already narrow security-planning window. Had that ceiling been cleared for release? No. It was protected.
beats.reveal_note: Neri's firsthand account proves that the seventh page materially assisted the hostile negotiators and prejudiced security planning. It does not identify who knowingly included it.

beats.speaker: w2

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: You asked Sela to update page seven that afternoon?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: Yes. The figures were stale, and keeping the internal master accurate was her job.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: You didn't ask her to prepare it for this exchange?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: No. It was internal and excluded from my six-file release sheet.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Did Sela ever tell you she'd send it?

turns.speaker: w2
turns.text: No, she didn't.

beats.text: You asked Sela to update page seven that afternoon? Yes. The figures were stale, and keeping the internal master accurate was her job. You didn't ask her to prepare it for this exchange? No. It was internal and excluded from my six-file release sheet. Did Sela ever tell you she'd send it? No, she didn't.
beats.reveal_note: Neri supplied a firsthand, lawful reason for the edits that the prosecution had treated as suspicious and confirmed that page seven was excluded from the approved package.

beats.speaker: w3

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: What material did you examine?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: Read-only images of Sela's workstation and the secure gateway, plus two support tickets exported by Halen. I verified their hashes and timestamps against the secure records.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: What could those records reliably show?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: The account in use, saved file versions, the package manifest, and transmission times.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: What couldn't they show?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: What a person actually noticed on screen.

beats.text: What material did you examine? Read-only images of Sela's workstation and the secure gateway, plus two support tickets exported by Halen. I verified their hashes and timestamps against the secure records. What could those records reliably show? The account in use, saved file versions, the package manifest, and transmission times. What couldn't they show? What a person actually noticed on screen.
beats.reveal_note: Dr Lell authenticated the digital records, explained their custody and integrity, and qualified the crucial limit: logs cannot reveal what Sela perceived or intended.

beats.speaker: w3

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Did you test the alleged export fault?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: Yes. On an isolated copy, I selected the same six file types.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: What happened?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: Page seven travelled through an old package link, but the confirmation screen still listed six files. Two earlier support tickets described the same fault.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Can the charged audit distinguish that fault from a deliberate attachment?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: No. The audit pattern is the same.

beats.text: Did you test the alleged export fault? Yes. On an isolated copy, I selected the same six file types. What happened? Page seven travelled through an old package link, but the confirmation screen still listed six files. Two earlier support tickets described the same fault. Can the charged audit distinguish that fault from a deliberate attachment? No. The audit pattern is the same.
beats.reveal_note: The authenticated system copy reproduced a silent inherited attachment, and contemporaneous support tickets proved it pre-dated this case. The charged audit cannot distinguish accident from choice.

beats.speaker: w3

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: What does the revision history show?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: Sela's account changed three figures on page seven eleven minutes before transmission. No other file changed.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Were those changes accurate?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: Yes. They made the negotiating ceiling current.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Could the export fault have made them?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: No. Those edits were manual.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: Could Sela still have known that the old link remained?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: It's possible. The records can't tell us whether she did.

beats.text: What does the revision history show? Sela's account changed three figures on page seven eleven minutes before transmission. No other file changed. Were those changes accurate? Yes. They made the negotiating ceiling current. Could the export fault have made them? No. Those edits were manual. Could Sela still have known that the old link remained? It's possible. The records can't tell us whether she did.
beats.reveal_note: The timing feels incriminating, but Neri assigned the corrections as ordinary work. Manual editing does not establish that Sela knew the separate export fault would carry the page.

beats.speaker: w3

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: You can't say Sela saw page seven listed for export?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: No. It wasn't listed.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Can edit history show why she edited it, or whether she knew an old link remained?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: No. It shows the account, session, edits, and timing. Not purpose, attention, or knowledge.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Did you find a message from Sela telling the recipient about page seven?

turns.speaker: w3
turns.text: No, I didn't.

beats.text: You can't say Sela saw page seven listed for export? No. It wasn't listed. Can edit history show why she edited it, or whether she knew an old link remained? No. It shows the account, session, edits, and timing. Not purpose, attention, or knowledge. Did you find a message from Sela telling the recipient about page seven? No, I didn't.
beats.reveal_note: The authenticated records contain no recipient note and cannot prove Sela saw, knew about, or deliberately used the inherited attachment. That missing mental-state link is central.

beats.speaker: acc

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Take us through the last part of your shift.

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: Neri asked me to fix three stale figures in the internal master. I did that, then opened Halen's cleared package.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: What appeared before you sent it?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: Six approved filenames and the authorised channel. I didn't see page seven.

turns.speaker: dc
turns.text: Did you mean to help the hostile authority?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: No. I meant to send the six negotiation briefs.

beats.text: Take us through the last part of your shift. Neri asked me to fix three stale figures in the internal master. I did that, then opened Halen's cleared package. What appeared before you sent it? Six approved filenames and the authorised channel. I didn't see page seven. Did you mean to help the hostile authority? No. I meant to send the six negotiation briefs.
beats.reveal_note: Sela's account is consistent with the release sheet, Neri's assignment, and the reproduced fault, although the jury need not accept her denial merely because she gave it.

beats.speaker: acc

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: You knew the account belonged to the hostile authority?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: Of course. That's where the authorised talks were held.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: You'd signed a warning about that account?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: Yes.

turns.speaker: pc
turns.text: And eleven minutes after correcting the secret limit, you clicked send?

turns.speaker: acc
turns.text: I corrected my assigned draft, then sent Halen's package. Those facts are true. I didn't know they were linked.

beats.text: You knew the account belonged to the hostile authority? Of course. That's where the authorised talks were held. You'd signed a warning about that account? Yes. And eleven minutes after correcting the secret limit, you clicked send? I corrected my assigned draft, then sent Halen's package. Those facts are true. I didn't know they were linked.
beats.reveal_note: Sela's knowledge of the recipient, her manual edits, and the close timing form the prosecution's strongest inference. They remain consistent with sending the six authorised briefs after routine editing.

beats.speaker: judge
beats.text: The parties agree an armed conflict existed and page seven prejudiced security planning. You decide whether Sela knew the protected page was included and intended the assistance. Editing page seven and sending six lawful briefs aren't enough unless the prosecution proves that further link. If, after considering all the evidence, you aren't sure every element was proved beyond reasonable doubt, your verdict must be Not Guilty.
beats.reveal_note: The fictional statute requires intentional assistance and knowledge of security prejudice. The agreed harm cannot replace proof that Sela knew the seventh page was travelling.

twist: The reference resolution is Not Guilty because the authenticated manifest showed six authorised files, a known fault silently carried page seven, and Sela had been assigned to correct the internal master. The strongest opposing interpretation is serious: she knew the recipient, improved the protected page, and sent the package eleven minutes later. But the records cannot show that she saw or knew about the hidden attachment, so that timing does not prove intentional assistance beyond reasonable doubt.

jurors.label: Ari
jurors.persona: Keeps returning to the element that is least securely proved, even when the consequences are unsettling.

agree: Yes, that's the gap: did she know page seven was in there?
pushback: Caro, I'm not ignoring the timing. I'm asking what it proves.
concede: I accept that clicking send was deliberate. The package contents are the harder question.
burden_drift: The harm makes an accident feel impossible, even when it isn't.
burden_correct: We don't have to explain the accident. The prosecution has to exclude it.
final: I'm still not sure Sela knew the seventh page travelled. That means Not Guilty for me.

jurors.label: Maren
jurors.persona: Starts with the suspicious sequence but changes course when a record cannot support the inference placed on it.

agree: Eleven minutes is close. Why should I treat that as coincidence?
pushback: Hang on—does the audit show a seventh selection, or are we adding one?
concede: All right, Dev. The same log appears when the fault fires. I'd missed that.
burden_drift: The page arrived, so part of me wants Sela to prove she didn't see it.
burden_correct: A system record isn't a mind-reading device. Dr Lell was clear about that.
final: I began at Guilty. The six-file screen and identical fault pattern have moved me.

jurors.label: Dev
jurors.persona: Tests each confident claim against the witness's actual words and is comfortable correcting an early impression.

agree: The timing does support the prosecution. I don't think we can wave it away.
pushback: Sorry, can someone show me where the screen displayed seven files? I can't find it.
concede: Wait—I had the sequence backwards. Neri requested the edit before Halen's package was opened.
burden_drift: Maybe I'm treating a terrible outcome as proof of a terrible intention.
burden_correct: Ari's right about one thing: possibility isn't proof, but a reasonable possibility matters.
final: I've changed my view. The records leave me unsure about knowledge, not about the harm.

jurors.label: Lio
jurors.persona: Reacts strongly to the human story, then checks that reaction against the manifest and the judge's direction.

agree: Six names on the screen and seven files sent—that's not a small detail.
pushback: But why edit only that page right before sending? I keep coming back to that.
concede: No, Maren, you're right—the edit request explains the timing better than I first allowed.
burden_drift: I want a clean answer from Sela, and real mistakes don't usually give us one.
burden_correct: The judge didn't say she must prove a mistake. We decide whether the state disproved it.
final: The system hid the extra page. I can't say Sela somehow saw what the screen didn't show.

jurors.label: Caro
jurors.persona: Trusts the close sequence of deliberate acts more than Sela's account, but accepts that carelessness is not treason.

agree: She knew the destination, fixed the useful page, then sent it. That's a real chain.
pushback: Why are we treating an experienced specialist as though she never checks her work?
concede: Fine, the warning proves who owned the account. It doesn't prove she knew every attachment.
burden_drift: If this was a mistake, it was an appalling one. I know that's not the legal test.
burden_correct: Carelessness, even serious carelessness, isn't the intention this charge requires.
final: I still read the timing as deliberate. I think the prosecution has proved Guilty.

jurors.label: Tess
jurors.persona: Separates a person's politics from their conduct and challenges the room when either side overstates a witness.

agree: Knowing the destination matters. It just doesn't answer knowledge of page seven.
pushback: Can we stop using her peace views as shorthand for what she did?
concede: Caro has a point about the timing. I give it weight—just not enough weight.
burden_drift: In wartime, criticism can start sounding like a confession. It isn't one.
burden_correct: Sela doesn't have to prove loyalty. The prosecution has to prove intentional assistance.
final: I believe the disclosure caused harm. I don't believe intention was proved beyond reasonable doubt.

jurors.label: Rami
jurors.persona: Begins sceptical of the defence but follows the examiner's limitations even when they complicate a neat story.

agree: The manual edit and the send were both hers. The dispute is the link between them.
pushback: No, Lio—the fault doesn't excuse everything. It explains one specific hidden attachment.
concede: Dr Lell couldn't distinguish the charged log from the reproduced fault. That changes my view.
burden_drift: I'm tempted to assume expertise means she must have noticed. The records don't say that.
burden_correct: We can infer knowledge, but the inference still has to exclude the documented alternative.
final: The technical evidence is stronger for reasonable doubt than I expected at the start.

jurors.label: Noa
jurors.persona: Voices the uncomfortable assumption beneath the room's argument, then revises it when another juror identifies the burden error.

agree: They used the limit four days later. Doesn't that make deliberate help more likely?
pushback: I'm lost—are we deciding whether Sela caused harm, or whether she knew?
concede: Right. Neri proved the harm, not Sela's state of mind. I was merging those.
burden_drift: But if Sela didn't know, shouldn't she be able to tell us exactly how it happened?
burden_correct: No—sorry. Ari's right. She doesn't carry that burden.
final: I needed the two questions separated. Once they are, I'm not sure about intention.

jurors.label: Iven
jurors.persona: Accepts official evidence only after its source, purpose, and limits have each been tested in court.

agree: Neri heard the precise ceiling used. I accept material assistance and actual prejudice.
pushback: Mika, which authenticated record shows that Sela selected page seven? There isn't one.
concede: I concede the short timing supports an inference. It just isn't the only reasonable one.
burden_drift: A protected label can make us assume intention before we examine the transmission.
burden_correct: Proof that information mattered is separate from proof that Sela knowingly sent it.
final: The custody is sound. The inference about Sela's knowledge is not sound enough for conviction.

jurors.label: Mika
jurors.persona: Finds the prosecution's chronology compelling and keeps testing whether the fault truly explains that coincidence.

agree: She made the useful information current and sent it minutes later. That's not nothing.
pushback: Iven, there may be no seventh click, but do we really need one to infer knowledge?
concede: The six-file confirmation is stronger than I thought. I'll give the defence that.
burden_drift: Maybe I'm filling the blank in the log with what happened afterward.
burden_correct: We can't turn suspicious timing into a presumption, but we can still weigh it.
final: For me, the sequence is too tight to be accidental. I remain at Guilty.

jurors.label: Sorin · foreperson
jurors.persona: Keeps the discussion organised without pretending disagreement has disappeared or forcing an undecided juror to choose.

agree: Let's write down the prosecution's chain: edit, warning, send, then use of the limit.
pushback: One at a time. Caro, what evidence answers the six-file confirmation screen?
concede: I was joining two deliberate acts together. The fault means that link needs its own proof.
burden_drift: The consequences are pulling us toward a result before we've finished the elements.
burden_correct: We can agree on harm and still disagree on knowledge. The prosecution must prove both.
final: We have honest disagreement. My own doubt is whether Sela knew the hidden page was attached.
